what: One table of folder paths, and what each side of the mirror says about one.
why: `cleanFolder` in app/src/core/paths.ts mirrors `resolve_within` in src/vault.rs
segment by segment, and a mirror is a thing that can drift. It exists because
the check has to happen before `fetch` rewrites the URL and before a
case-folding filesystem rewrites the path — neither of which the server can
see — so the duplication is deliberate. This file is what stops the two copies
drifting without anyone noticing: each side reads its own column and must
still answer what is written here.
Containment only. The client additionally refuses a folder the INDEX would not
draw (`templates/`, `daily/`), which is a rule about what counts as a note and
not about where the vault ends — so every accepted case here is also a folder
the INDEX lists, and listedness is tested on its own in paths.test.ts.
The server is asked about `<path>/x.md`, because `resolve_within` judges a path
to a file and a folder is only ever reached through one.
`server` and `client` are separate columns because on two rows they disagree,
and a single verdict would have had to hide that. Rust's `Path::components`
normalises an empty component away, so the server reads `notes//x.md` as
`notes/x.md` and accepts it; `cleanFolder` splits on `/` and refuses the empty
segment. Both land inside the vault and on the same file, so this is a
difference in strictness rather than a hole — recorded here so it is a
decision rather than a surprise.
